title: Fast Unsupervised Deep Outlier Model Selection with Hypernetworks

problem.claim: Effective hyperparameter tuning and model selection for unsupervised deep outlier detection.

gap.claim: Unsupervised validation lacks labeled outliers, while modern deep outlier detection models have many hyperparameters that make search inefficient.

contributions.claim: HYPER uses a hypernetwork to map hyperparameters to optimal weights for the main outlier detection model.
HYPER uses one hypernetwork to dynamically generate weights for multiple outlier detection models across hyperparameter settings.
HYPER uses meta-learning on labeled historical outlier detection tasks to train a proxy validation function.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report significant speed-up from dynamically generating weights for many models with a single hypernetwork.
The authors report that HYPER achieves competitive performance against eight baselines with significant efficiency gains on different outlier detection tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Deep neural network-based outlier detection has recently attracted increased attention.
The paper focuses on unsupervised hyperparameter tuning and model selection, which is difficult because of absent labels and expanding hyperparameter spaces.
HYPER uses a hypernetwork to generate model weights across hyperparameter settings and meta-learning to construct a proxy validation function.
Experiments on different outlier detection tasks are reported to show competitive performance against eight baselines and efficiency gains.

unknowns: The specific outlier detection tasks, datasets, metrics, and experimental settings are not provided.
The eight baselines and quantitative performance or efficiency results are not provided.
The hypernetwork architecture, training procedure, and proxy validation function details are not provided.
